page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores running on an AWS Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes a substantial 1875 GB NVMe SSD local storage volume. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, scoring 1519.89 and 6054.65 respectively. However, memory and computational benchmarks show limitations, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores falling into the weak category. Cryptographic and compression tasks also register lower tiers, as evidenced by a poor Passmark CPU encryption score of 539.37 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.32 GB/sec. Large block memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only speeds at 69.63 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.78 GB/sec.

The im4gn.xlarge offers high local storage density relative to its compute footprint, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for storage-heavy workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. The primary tradeoff is the lower CPU and memory performance compared to newer architectures, as reflected in the poor Passmark database operations and weak Redis SET performance of 4.92 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for storage-intensive applications, local caching, and database workloads with moderate compute demands.

Benchmark data shows average stress-ng CPU performance but weak overall computational and memory scores, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3191.0 and a weak Redis SET throughput of 4.92 million operations per second. The instance presents a clear tradeoff, offering high storage density per vCPU at the expense of raw processing power. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-heavy applications and moderate database workloads that benefit from local NVMe SSD capacity rather than high-performance compute.
